str-driving.source: Stroke Foundation (Australia), Driving after stroke, which gives at least four weeks for a private licence and three months for a commercial one, with medical clearance required before returning, and two weeks (four, commercial) after a transient ischaemic attack. The underlying standard is Austroads, Assessing Fitness to Drive
str-driving.note: The presentation gave three weeks for a private licence. The Australian standard is four. This is the one number on the page that was changed rather than attributed, because a patient told three weeks would be driving unlicensed and uninsured in the fourth.

ext-wipo-share.claim: Weaning-induced pulmonary oedema accounted for 59 per cent of weaning failures (75 of 128 failed spontaneous breathing trials, across 283 trials in 81 patients)
ext-wipo-share.source: Liu J et al, Cardiac dysfunction induced by weaning from mechanical ventilation: incidence, risk factors and effects of fluid removal, Critical Care 2016;20:369. Single-centre observational study

ext-wipo-risk.claim: Independent risk factors for weaning-induced pulmonary oedema: COPD odds ratio 8.7 (95% CI 2.0-37.3), structural cardiopathy 4.5 (1.4-14.1), obesity 3.6 (1.2-12.6)
ext-wipo-risk.source: Liu J et al, Critical Care 2016;20:369. The authors describe the obesity association as weaker than the other two and in need of confirmation

ext-diaphragm.claim: Diaphragm dysfunction at weaning: reported incidence 23 to 80 per cent depending on population and method; 29 per cent by ultrasound at first spontaneous breathing trial, 63 per cent by phrenic nerve stimulation in unselected patients
ext-diaphragm.source: Dres M and Demoule A, Diaphragm dysfunction during weaning from mechanical ventilation, Critical Care 2018;22:73, citing Kim et al and Dres et al

ext-reintubation-mortality.claim: Hospital mortality 18 per cent in reintubated patients against 3 per cent in those never reintubated; adjusted odds ratio 5.86 (95% CI 3.87-8.89). 19 per cent reintubated at some point, 11 per cent within 48 hours
ext-reintubation-mortality.source: Cohort of 2,007 patients reported in Respiratory Care 2012;57:1555. The authors caution this is association, not proof of causation, and that reintubation partly marks greater severity

ext-niv-rescue.claim: Non-invasive ventilation for established post-extubation respiratory failure: reintubation 48 per cent in both arms; median time from failure to intubation 2.5 hours with usual care against 12 hours with NIV; ICU mortality 14 against 25 per cent (RR 1.78, 95% CI 1.03-3.20, p=0.048). Trial stopped early
ext-niv-rescue.source: Esteban A et al, Noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation for respiratory failure after extubation, NEJM 2004;350:2452. Read through a published summary of the trial; the original could not be reached from this environment

ext-niv-prophylactic.claim: Prophylactic non-invasive ventilation alternating with high-flow nasal oxygen in high-risk patients: reintubation at day 7 11.8 against 18.2 per cent with high-flow alone (difference -6.4 per cent, 95% CI -12.0 to -0.9, p=0.02). ICU mortality 6 against 9 per cent, not significant
ext-niv-prophylactic.source: Thille AW et al, JAMA 2019;322:1465. High risk defined as ventilated over 24 hours, passed a spontaneous breathing trial, and over 65 or with underlying cardiac or respiratory disease including obesity hypoventilation

ext-steroid-cuffleak.claim: Corticosteroids before extubation in patients selected by a failed cuff leak test: reintubation RR 0.35 (95% CI 0.20-0.64), post-extubation respiratory failure RR 0.34 (0.24-0.48), NNT 5. In unselected patients neither reached significance. The cuff leak test has poor positive predictive value for stridor
ext-steroid-cuffleak.source: 2017 meta-analysis of 11 randomised trials, 2,472 patients. Regimens included methylprednisolone 40 mg 6-hourly for four doses, or a single 40 mg dose 4 hours before extubation

cm-ici-steroid.claim: Immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis is treated with pulse methylprednisolone 500 to 1000 mg daily for three to five days
cm-ici-steroid.source: ESC/EHA/ESTRO/IC-OS cardio-oncology guidance as summarised in Cardiovascular Diagnosis and Therapy, 'Therapeutic agents for steroid-refractory immune checkpoint inhibitor-related myocarditis'. ESMO gives three days; NCCN and SITC give 1 g for three to five

cm-ici-refractory.claim: What proportion of immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis is steroid-refractory
cm-ici-refractory.source: No population-level estimate exists: the review states that no studies have estimated the incidence of steroid-refractory disease, and the only figure available is a single-centre series of 24 patients in which 16 (67 per cent) were corticosteroid-resistant. This page previously said 'up to half', which was not supported by anything, and has been reworded

nn-adrenaline.claim: Adrenaline 10 to 30 micrograms/kg intravenously, which is 0.1 to 0.3 mL/kg of 1:10,000, repeated every 3 to 5 minutes while the heart rate stays below 60. The endotracheal dose is higher at 50 to 100 micrograms/kg, and the umbilical vein is the suggested route
nn-adrenaline.source: ANZCOR neonatal guidelines 13.1 to 13.8, collected edition

nn-volume.claim: Volume expansion 10 mL/kg of isotonic crystalloid, for suspected blood loss or shock that has not responded to other measures, given over several minutes and repeated after reassessment
nn-volume.source: ANZCOR neonatal guidelines 13.1 to 13.8, collected edition

nn-glucose.claim: Target blood glucose at least 2.6 mmol/L, with an intravenous bolus of 2 mL/kg of 10 per cent dextrose. Note that a cooled baby is managed to a higher range, 3 to 7 mmol/L
nn-glucose.source: WA Child and Adolescent Health Service / NETS WA, Hypoglycaemia

nn-cooling.claim: Therapeutic hypothermia for moderate or severe hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy at 35 weeks or more and under 6 hours of age. The full NSW criteria add a weight of at least 1,800 g and evidence of perinatal depression — pH below 7.00, base excess -12 or worse, Apgar under 6 at 10 minutes, or resuscitation lasting 10 minutes or more
nn-cooling.source: NSW Agency for Clinical Innovation, Hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy in newborns

nn-pge.claim: Alprostadil from 10 nanograms/kg/min, range 5 to 50. Doses of 50 or more may be needed to resuscitate an infant with poor perfusion and oxygenation, or where the duct is constricting or already closed. Maintenance is then the lowest dose that holds it open, usually 3 to 20
nn-pge.source: Royal Hospital for Women neonatal formulary, Alprostadil v3.0, September 2025
